content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using annual data lagged at least 6 months. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Inventory accumulating faster than sales signals weak demand and future markdowns/write-offs, foreshadowing lower earnings and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Intensity", "construction": "Order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by total assets (item AT), measured annually with a 6-month reporting lag. Sort stocks into quintiles.", "rationale": "A large backlog relative to firm size reflects contracted future revenue not yet in reported earnings, which the market underweights.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Cash Productivity", "construction": "Cash and short-term investments (item CHE) divided by market value of equity (price times shares outstanding). Rank cross-sectionally each June using fiscal year-end data lagged 6 months.", "rationale": "Firms with large cash relative to market cap are undervalued and possess financial flexibility to invest or return capital, earning higher subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Depreciation-to-Capex Gap", "construction": "Ratio of depreciation and amortization (item DP) to capital expenditures (item CAPX), annual data lagged 6 months. Higher ratio means the firm is under-investing relative to its asset consumption.", "rationale": "Firms whose capex lags depreciation are harvesting assets, often a value trap, whereas heavy reinvestors relative to depreciation may over-invest; the middle-to-high harvesting group tends to be cheap and mean-revert upward.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (harvesting firms)"}, {"name": "Accrual-to-Cashflow Wedge", "construction": "Compute total accruals as change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by absolute operating cash flow (from funds statement items). Rank firms; those with the lowest accruals relative to cash flow are highest quality.", "rationale": "Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash flow are less persistent, so low-accrual firms deliver higher future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low accruals)"}, {"name": "Selling Expense Efficiency Change", "construction": "Year-over-year change in the ratio of SG&A expense (item XSGA) to sales (item SALE). Firms reducing SG&A intensity are improving operating leverage. Annual data lagged 6 months.", "rationale": "Declining overhead intensity signals margin expansion and disciplined management that the market prices slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "low (declining) values of the change"}, {"name": "Return Convexity Around Zero", "construction": "Using 36 months of trailing monthly returns, count the fraction of months with returns within +/-2% of zero (low-volatility clustering) versus large moves. Rank firms by this stability fraction.", "rationale": "Stocks with returns tightly clustered near zero are neglected and low-beta, and neglect premia plus lottery-avoidance drive higher future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (more stability)"}, {"name": "Dividend Coverage Buffer", "construction": "Earnings per share (item EPS) minus dividends per share (item DVPSX) scaled by price, i.e., retained earnings yield. Annual data lagged 6 months. Sort into quintiles.", "rationale": "A wide gap between earnings and dividends means the payout is safe and internally funded growth is available, both of which support higher subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Asset Turnover Acceleration", "construction": "Second difference of asset turnover: (SALE/AT this year minus last year) minus (SALE/AT last year minus year before). Positive acceleration indicates improving asset utilization. Annual data lagged 6 months.", "rationale": "Accelerating efficiency reflects operational momentum in fundamentals that anticipates earnings surprises the market underreacts to.", "higher_returns_for": "high (positive) values of the measure"}, {"name": "Relative Trading Volume Contraction", "construction": "Ratio of average monthly share turnover (volume/shares outstanding) over the most recent 3 months to that over the prior 12 months. Values below one indicate declining attention. Use CRSP volume data.", "rationale": "Falling turnover marks investor neglect and reduced liquidity attention; such neglected stocks subsequently earn a premium as attention returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (contracting volume)"}]}
